stem: A nurse notes that a central venous catheter dressing has become loose and no longer fully covers the insertion site. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Replace the compromised dressing promptly using appropriate aseptic catheter-site care according to facility policy.
options.B: Leave it in place until the routine scheduled dressing change because looseness alone is not an indication for replacement.
options.C: Tape over the loose edges without reassessing or replacing the dressing because preserving the old dressing is preferred.
options.D: Remove the central venous catheter solely because the dressing is loose, even if the catheter remains clinically indicated and the site has no other complication.

rationale: A is correct. CDC recommends replacing a catheter-site dressing whenever it becomes damp, loosened, or visibly soiled and covering catheter sites with sterile gauze or a sterile transparent semipermeable dressing. A loose dressing compromises the protective barrier and should not be left until the next routine interval. B and C fail to restore an intact dressing. D overreacts: a loose dressing requires prompt dressing replacement, but catheter removal is based on catheter necessity and complications rather than looseness of the dressing alone.
educational_objective: Maintain central-line site protection by promptly replacing any dressing that becomes loose, damp, or visibly soiled using appropriate aseptic site-care technique rather than waiting for the routine interval or removing an otherwise needed catheter solely for dressing failure.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Guidelines for the Prevention of Intravascular Catheter-Related Infections — Summary of Recommendations; Prevention Strategies
source_version_date: Current CDC infection-control web guidance accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Catheter Site Dressing Regimens: use sterile gauze or sterile transparent semipermeable dressing to cover the site; replace catheter-site dressing if it becomes damp, loosened, or visibly soiled (Category IB). Central-line maintenance recommendations also emphasize continued assessment of catheter necessity and insertion-site condition.
source_claim_supported: A central-line dressing that becomes loose should be replaced promptly with an intact sterile dressing using appropriate catheter-site care; looseness alone does not automatically require removal of a clinically necessary catheter.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: maintain invasive devices using aseptic technique and implement measures that reduce healthcare-associated infection risk.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — central-line dressing integrity
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source item as a catheter-maintenance safety decision and corrected the blueprint from Basic Care and Comfort to Safety and Infection Prevention and Control. Avoided the unsupported claim that every loose dressing necessarily increases infection in a quantifiable way; the final action is anchored to the direct CDC replacement recommendation.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against current CDC catheter-site dressing recommendations.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A directly follows the loosened-dressing replacement recommendation. B delays required care. C does not restore the recommended dressing barrier. D confuses a maintenance problem with an automatic catheter-removal indication.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; replace promptly with appropriate aseptic site care.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; looseness is an explicit replacement indication.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; simply reinforcing a compromised dressing is not the recommended replacement action.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; catheter removal depends on necessity/complications, not dressing looseness alone.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A addresses the actual dressing problem while preserving the catheter if still indicated.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are competing central-line maintenance actions.
audit_findings.blueprint: Device-associated infection prevention fits Safety and Infection Prevention and Control.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked dressing-replacement indication, catheter-removal criteria, and sterile/aseptic wording. No unsupported timing interval or second answer remained.
